tier1.text: The lateral rectus moves the eye away from the nose. The lateral rectus is one of six extraocular muscles, the muscles that move the eye. Lateral means toward the side, and this muscle lies on the outer side of the eyeball. The abducens nerve, one of the cranial nerves connected to the brain, controls this muscle.

quotes.quote: Four of the muscles are arranged at the cardinal points around the eye and are named for those locations. They are the superior rectus, medial rectus, inferior rectus, and lateral rectus.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: The extraocular muscles are innervated by three cranial nerves. The lateral rectus, which causes abduction of the eye, is innervated by the abducens nerve.
